research_summary: HUBMASTER manufactures and integrates multi aisle stacker crane ASRS, differentiated by one crane serving many aisles, its own HmWare control software, and a no battery advantage that is especially strong in cold storage. After rebranding in Jan 2024 and relocating to the DFactory Barcelona innovation hub, it is pushing hard into North America, evidenced by a Chicago office and back to back US trade show appearances (MODEX 2024, ProMat 2025). Its content consistently targets the labor shortage and cold storage pains its buyers feel. As a differentiated but still growing brand expanding in a new region, its constraint is getting in front of enough warehouse and operations leaders to fill a long, complex project pipeline.

title: Founder & CEO
research_signals: Recently built out a full executive bench: Founder/CEO Jimy Mertune, COO Humberto Villasenor (P.E.), CFO Naz Kabir and CTO Anil Gunda | Hiring a VP role based in Orlando, signaling an active scaling phase | Domestic US solar panel manufacturer positioning on made in America versus imports, claiming 25.2 percent efficiency and targeting 1GW capacity within 5 years | Actively raising capital via a dedicated Investor page (projected 35 percent two year ROI); note the published figures such as 1.14B in revenue are self reported and look aggressive for an early stage manufacturer, worth verifying before leaning on them | CEO active locally (met Orlando Mayor Buddy Dyer, May 2025) and also works as a mortgage loan consultant at J&R Funding
research_summary: ShineGreen Energy is an early stage domestic US solar panel manufacturer in Orlando, positioning on made in America quality versus imports and targeting 1GW of capacity within five years. It has just stood up a full executive team (COO, CFO, CTO) and is hiring a VP in Orlando, clear signs of an active scaling phase, while raising capital. One caution for outreach: the investor page projections (for example 1.14B revenue at a 63 percent net margin) are self reported and look aggressive for a company at this stage, so treat them as claims rather than facts. The credible, referenceable hook is the scaling story: a young manufacturer building a team and capacity that now needs commercial demand, meaning installers and EPCs, to grow with it.
